title: An hour of babysitting
setting: A Saturday morning outside Kenta's building. Kenta is minding his sister's month-old baby for the first time, and it won't stop crying. Satou-san, the elderly neighbour, comes out and hears it.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: nakanaide, nakanaide. sugu kaette kuru kara ne.
lines.ja: 泣かないで、泣かないで。すぐ帰ってくるからね。
lines.kana: なかないで、なかないで。すぐかえってくるからね。
lines.english: Don't cry, don't cry. She'll be back soon, okay?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: kenta-san, ohayou gozaimasu. are? okosan ga ita n desu ka?
lines.ja: ケンタさん、おはようございます。あれ？お子さんがいたんですか？
lines.kana: けんたさん、おはようございます。あれ？おこさんがいたんですか？
lines.english: Good morning, Kenta-san. Oh? I didn't know you had a child.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: a, ohayou gozaimasu. iya, boku wa kodomo inai desu yo. sengetsu, ane ni kodomo ga umareta n desu.
lines.ja: あ、おはようございます。いや、僕は子供いないですよ。先月、姉に子供が生まれたんです。
lines.kana: あ、おはようございます。いや、ぼくはこどもいないですよ。せんげつ、あねにこどもがうまれたんです。
lines.english: Oh, good morning. No, I don't have any kids. My sister had a baby last month.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: aa, oneesan no okosan desu ka. omedetou gozaimasu.
lines.ja: ああ、お姉さんのお子さんですか。おめでとうございます。
lines.kana: ああ、おねえさんのおこさんですか。おめでとうございます。
lines.english: Ah, it's your sister's little one. Congratulations.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu. ane, kodomo ga umarete kara, zutto jikan ga nakute. kyou yatto, kami kiri ni itteru n desu.
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。姉、子供が生まれてから、ずっと時間がなくて。今日やっと、髪切りに行ってるんです。
lines.kana: ありがとうございます。あね、こどもがうまれてから、ずっとじかんがなくて。きょうやっと、かみきりにいってるんです。
lines.english: Thank you. Since the baby came, my sister hasn't had a minute to herself. Today she's finally gone to get her hair cut.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sore de, kenta-san ga mendou o miteru n desu ka. demo, sugoku naitemasu ne.
lines.ja: それで、ケンタさんが面倒を見てるんですか。でも、すごく泣いてますね。
lines.kana: それで、けんたさんがめんどうをみてるんですか。でも、すごくないてますね。
lines.english: So that's why you're looking after the baby. The little one's really crying, though.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sou na n desu. ane ga dete, mada ichijikan na n desu kedo. kodomo sodateru no tte, taihen desu ne.
lines.ja: そうなんです。姉が出て、まだ一時間なんですけど。子供育てるのって、大変ですね。
lines.kana: そうなんです。あねがでて、まだいちじかんなんですけど。こどもそだてるのって、たいへんですね。
lines.english: It is. My sister's only been gone an hour, but raising kids sure is hard work.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: haha. kodomo ga otona ni naru made, nijuunen arimasu yo. chotto, ii desu ka?
lines.ja: はは。子供が大人になるまで、二十年ありますよ。ちょっと、いいですか？
lines.kana: はは。こどもがおとなになるまで、にじゅうねんありますよ。ちょっと、いいですか？
lines.english: Ha ha. It's twenty years until a child grows up, you know. May I?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.ja: ね？もう泣いてないでしょう？
lines.kana: ね？もうないてないでしょう？

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e, sugoi! satou-san, okosan iru n desu ka?
lines.ja: え、すごい！佐藤さん、お子さんいるんですか？
lines.kana: え、すごい！さとうさん、おこさんいるんですか？
lines.english: Wow, amazing! Satou-san, do you have kids?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: hai, sannin imasu yo. minna mou otona ni natte, uchi o demashita kedo ne.
lines.ja: はい、三人いますよ。みんなもう大人になって、うちを出ましたけどね。
lines.kana: はい、さんにんいますよ。みんなもうおとなになって、うちをでましたけどね。
lines.english: Yes, three. They're all grown up now and have left home, mind you.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sannin mo! kodomo sannin sodateta n desu ka. sugoi naa.
lines.ja: 三人も！子供三人育てたんですか。すごいなあ。
lines.kana: さんにんも！こどもさんにんそだてたんですか。すごいなあ。
lines.english: Three! You raised three kids? That's amazing.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: iya iya, kodomo no mendou o miteta no wa, zutto tsuma datta n desu. watashi wa shigoto bakkari de.
lines.ja: いやいや、子供の面倒を見てたのは、ずっと妻だったんです。私は仕事ばっかりで。
lines.kana: いやいや、こどものめんどうをみてたのは、ずっとつまだったんです。わたしはしごとばっかりで。
lines.english: Oh no, no. It was always my wife who looked after the kids. I was working all the time.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e? demo, ima no, sugokatta desu yo.
lines.ja: え？でも、今の、すごかったですよ。
lines.kana: え？でも、いまの、すごかったですよ。
lines.english: Really? But what you just did was amazing.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: mago ga umarete kara, maishuu mendou o miteru n desu. kodomo o sodateru no ga taihen da tte, yatto wakarimashita yo.
lines.ja: 孫が生まれてから、毎週面倒を見てるんです。子供を育てるのが大変だって、やっと分かりましたよ。
lines.kana: まごがうまれてから、まいしゅうめんどうをみてるんです。こどもをそだてるのがたいへんだって、やっとわかりましたよ。
lines.english: Since my grandchild was born, I've looked after them every week. Only now have I learned how hard it is to raise kids.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: jaa, ane ga kaette kuru made, mendou mite moraemasen ka? onegai shimasu!
lines.ja: じゃあ、姉が帰ってくるまで、面倒見てもらえませんか？お願いします！
lines.kana: じゃあ、あねがかえってくるまで、めんどうみてもらえませんか？おねがいします！
lines.english: Then could you look after the baby until my sister gets back? Please!

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: haha, ii desu yo. demo, kenta-san mo koko ni ite kudasai ne.
lines.ja: はは、いいですよ。でも、ケンタさんもここにいてくださいね。
lines.kana: はは、いいですよ。でも、けんたさんもここにいてくださいね。
lines.english: Ha ha, all right. But you're staying here too, Kenta-san.

choices.english: Kenta has just become a father, and Satou-san gives him tips on raising kids.
Satou-san asks Kenta to look after his grandchild for the morning.
Satou-san settles the baby Kenta is minding for his sister, and Kenta asks him to help until she's back.

questions.explanation: Line 3: the baby isn't Kenta's. He has no kids (kodomo inai), and his sister had a baby last month (ane ni kodomo ga umareta). Line 5: she has finally gone to get her hair cut, so Kenta is looking after the baby (line 6). Lines 8-10: Satou-san takes the baby and it stops crying (mou naitenai deshou?). Line 17: Kenta asks him to look after it until his sister gets back (mendou mite moraemasen ka?), and in line 18 he agrees, as long as Kenta stays too. A is wrong: Kenta says he has no kids (line 3), and the tips idea is turned on its head when Satou-san admits his wife did the looking after (line 14). B is wrong: Satou-san looks after his grandchild every week (line 16), but today it's Kenta who asks Satou-san for help.

questions.english: Satou-san gets talking with you outside the building and asks, "okosan wa iru n desu ka?" (Do you have children?) Answer him using kodomo and iru: say you don't have any, or how many you have.
questions.ja: お子さんはいるんですか？
questions.kana: おこさんはいるんですか？
questions.romaji: okosan wa iru n desu ka?
questions.answer: Use kodomo with iru, the verb for people: kodomo wa inai n desu (I don't have any), or kodomo ga hitori imasu (I have one), with the number after kodomo.

modelAnswers.romaji: iie, kodomo wa inai n desu.
modelAnswers.ja: いいえ、子供はいないんです。
modelAnswers.english: No, I don't have any children.

modelAnswers.romaji: hai, kodomo ga hitori imasu. sengetsu umareta n desu.
modelAnswers.ja: はい、子供が一人います。先月生まれたんです。
modelAnswers.english: Yes, I have one. Born just last month.

questions.explanation: Children, like brothers and sisters, take iru, the verb for people and animals. Don't use aru (for things) or kodomo o motte imasu (a word-for-word 'have'). Satou-san asks with iru in line 2 (okosan ga ita n desu ka?), Kenta answers kodomo inai in line 3 and asks okosan iru n desu ka? in line 11, and Satou-san answers sannin imasu in line 12, with the number before the verb. Say okosan for someone else's children and kodomo for your own. Satou-san speaks politely, so answer politely.

questions.english: When Satou-san asks if the baby is Kenta's, how does Kenta explain whose it is?
questions.ja: ケンタさんは、お姉さんのことを何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんたさんは、おねえさんのことをなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenta-san wa, oneesan no koto o nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: my sister 'had' a child (motsu, hold or own)
my sister had a baby (a baby was born to her)
my sister 'had' a child (aru, the verb for things)

questions.explanation: Line 3: 'sengetsu, ane ni kodomo ga umareta n desu.' The baby is the subject of umareru (be born) and the parent takes ni, which is how Japanese shares birth news. Kenta uses it again in line 5 (kodomo ga umarete kara, since the baby was born). A is wrong: kodomo o motsu is about being a parent as a stage of life (kodomo o motte kara, since becoming a parent), not news of a birth, and motta on its own sounds like she picked something up. C is wrong: aru is for things, and kodomo ga atta isn't said for having a baby.

questions.english: After one hour, Kenta says raising kids is hard work. Satou-san laughs and says, "kodomo ga otona ni naru made, nijuunen arimasu yo." What does he mean?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、何が言いたかったんですか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、なにがいいたかったんですか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, nani ga iitakatta n desu ka?

choices.english: Kenta has only just started: it takes twenty years for a child to grow up.
Kenta needs another twenty years before he's grown-up enough to have kids.
His own children grew up twenty years ago, so he's forgotten how hard it is.

questions.explanation: Line 8: otona ni naru is 'become an adult, grow up', and made is 'until', so a child takes twenty years to grow up. After Kenta's single hour (line 7), Satou-san is gently teasing him: the hard part has only just begun. In line 12 he uses it about his own children: minna mou otona ni natte (they're all grown up now). B is wrong: otona ni naru can also mean acting more grown-up, but the subject here is kodomo (a child), not Kenta. C is wrong: he never says when his children grew up, and in line 16 he says he has only now learned how hard raising kids is.

questions.english: That evening Kenta tells you, "kyou, zutto ane no kodomo no mendou miteta n da. tsukareta." (I was looking after my sister's baby all day. I'm worn out.) Sympathise using kodomo and sodateru: say raising kids must be tough.
questions.ja: 今日、ずっと姉の子供の面倒見てたんだ。疲れた。
questions.kana: きょう、ずっとあねのこどものめんどうみてたんだ。つかれた。
questions.romaji: kyou, zutto ane no kodomo no mendou miteta n da. tsukareta.
questions.answer: Say raising kids is tough with kodomo (o) sodateru and taihen: kodomo sodateru no tte taihen da yo ne. In casual speech o drops.

modelAnswers.romaji: otsukare! kodomo sodateru no tte, taihen da yo ne.
modelAnswers.ja: お疲れ！子供育てるのって、大変だよね。
modelAnswers.english: Well done! Raising kids is tough, isn't it.

modelAnswers.romaji: oneesan, mainichi kodomo sodateteru n da ne. sugoi naa.
modelAnswers.ja: お姉さん、毎日子供育ててるんだね。すごいなあ。
modelAnswers.english: And your sister's raising a kid every single day. Amazing.

questions.explanation: sodateru is raising children over the years, with kodomo as its object. Kenta says it in line 7 (kodomo sodateru no tte, taihen desu ne) and line 13 (kodomo sannin sodateta), and Satou-san in line 16 (kodomo o sodateru no ga taihen da tte). Its partner sodatsu is the child's side, growing up (toukyou de sodatta, I grew up in Tokyo), so it doesn't fit here. Kenta is your friend, so answer casually.

questions.english: Kenta tells you, "ashita mo ane ga kaimono ni iku n da kedo, boku, shigoto na n da. dou shiyou." (My sister's going shopping again tomorrow, but I've got work. What do I do?) Offer to look after the baby, using mendou and miru.
questions.ja: 明日も姉が買い物に行くんだけど、僕、仕事なんだ。どうしよう。
questions.kana: あしたもあねがかいものにいくんだけど、ぼく、しごとなんだ。どうしよう。
questions.romaji: ashita mo ane ga kaimono ni iku n da kedo, boku, shigoto na n da. dou shiyou.
questions.answer: Offer with mendou (o) miru: watashi ga mendou miru yo (I'll look after the baby), or the favour form mendou mite ageru yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, ashita wa watashi ga mendou miru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、明日は私が面倒見るよ。
modelAnswers.english: Then I'll look after the baby tomorrow.

modelAnswers.romaji: ii yo, kodomo no mendou nara mite ageru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: いいよ、子供の面倒なら見てあげるよ。
modelAnswers.english: Sure, I can look after the baby for you.

questions.explanation: mendou o miru is looking after someone and taking responsibility for them: babies, kids, grandchildren. Satou-san uses it in line 6 (kenta-san ga mendou o miteru), line 14 (kodomo no mendou o miteta) and line 16 (maishuu mendou o miteru), and Kenta asks for it in line 17 (mendou mite moraemasen ka?). In casual speech o drops (mendou miru). Don't mix it up with mendokusai (what a hassle): same mendou, opposite feel. Kenta is a friend, so casual is right.

newWords.english: someone else's child (polite; say kodomo for your own)
my older sister (oneesan: someone else's older sister)
cry (naiteru: is crying; nakanaide: don't cry)
until (ane ga kaette kuru made = until my sister gets back)
